Schools may read their own record (`GET /schools/me/commission`) but only `SUPER_ADMIN` can change it. Amounts are naira, matching `Transaction.amount`.

Creates a new class scoped to the authenticated user's school.

get.summary: Commission statistics (rate, totals, per-school and per-source breakdown)
get.description:
Aggregates the platform commission ledger. Every commissioned transaction writes an `EARNED` entry when it settles, and a `REVERSED` entry if that settlement is later undone — every figure here is net of reversals.

**Scope** — `SUPER_ADMIN` only. Commission is platform revenue, so school-side roles (`SCHOOL_ADMIN`, `FINANCE`) receive **403**. A platform admin sees every school by default and may narrow to one with `schoolId`.

**Rates** — `configuredRate` is what the platform charges today (`PAYMENT_COMMISSION` / `SMS_TOPUP_COMMISSION`), while `appliedRates` is what was actually charged in the requested window, so a rate change stays visible in history. `effectiveRatePercent` expresses commission as a share of what payers handed over.

Amounts are in the same unit as `Transaction.amount` (naira).

parameters.description: Platform admins only — restrict the report to one school.

parameters.description: Restrict to fee payments or SMS wallet top-ups.

parameters.name: schoolLimit
parameters.description: Cap on the `bySchool` breakdown, highest earning first.

patch.summary: Set what a school is charged per checkout
patch.description:
`SUPER_ADMIN` only — schools cannot edit their own rate.

**Applies from the next checkout.** Transactions already initiated keep the rate they were quoted, because it is stored on the transaction itself, so a rate change never rewrites what a parent was shown or what the ledger recorded.

`value` is read against `rateType`: naira per checkout for `FLAT`, a percentage of the checkout subtotal for `PERCENTAGE`. Switching to `PERCENTAGE` therefore requires sending `value` in the same request — carrying a flat ₦500 over as 500% is rejected. `minAmount` / `maxAmount` bound a percentage rate and are ignored for a flat one; send `null` to clear either. `isActive: false` charges the school's parents nothing without deleting the record.

value.description: Naira per checkout when FLAT; a percentage (2.5 = 2.5%) when PERCENTAGE.

minAmount.description: PERCENTAGE only — floor in naira. Null clears it.

maxAmount.description: PERCENTAGE only — ceiling in naira. Null clears it.

403.description: Role cannot manage commission — schools may read but not edit their rate

post.summary: Start an impersonation session
post.description:
Allows a SUPER_ADMIN to impersonate any non-SUPER_ADMIN user of any school.
Creates a new impersonation session record and returns a short-lived JWT
(default 2 h) signed with the target user's identity plus an impersonation
context block. All subsequent requests made with this token are automatically
logged to the `impersonation_logs` collection.
The caller's identity (impersonatorId + email) is embedded in the JWT so it
can never be spoofed by the token holder.

get.summary: Get the authenticated parent's wallet balance
get.description: Returns the credit balance held for the authenticated parent at their school. Balance accrues when a parent pays more than a student owed — an over-transfer to a dynamic virtual account, an over-collected cash payment, or an installment paid past the outstanding balance. Credit is scoped to the school it was earned at and can be applied to any of that parent's children in the same school. A parent with no wallet yet gets a zero-balance wallet created on first read.

404.description: Caller is not a registered parent

get.summary: List the authenticated parent's wallet movements
get.description: Append-only history of every credit and debit on the parent's wallet, newest first. `reason` explains the movement: `OVERPAYMENT` (money paid above a fee), `PAYMENT_APPLIED` (credit spent on a fee), `REFUND`, or `ADJUSTMENT`. `balanceAfter` is the wallet balance immediately after the entry was written.

post.summary: Settle fees from the parent's wallet credit
post.description: Applies wallet credit to one or more payment items for one of the parent's own children. No gateway is involved and no commission is charged — commission was already collected on the payment that created the credit. Each allocation is capped at what the item still owes, so credit is never over-applied; any remainder simply stays in the wallet. The wallet debit and the resulting transactions are written together, so a partial failure cannot leave the parent debited for fees that were never recorded.

studentId.description: Must be one of the authenticated parent's linked children.

400.description: Insufficient balance, or an item is already fully paid

post.summary: Record opening balances for many parents at once
post.description: Bulk form of the single top-up, for onboarding a school from a spreadsheet of parents who already carry a balance. Up to 500 rows per call. Rows are processed independently — a bad `parentId` or a parent from another school fails that row only and is returned under `failed`, so a school never has to work out which of several hundred rows landed. Each row is idempotent on its own `reference`, so a corrected sheet can be re-uploaded safely: rows already applied come back with `duplicate: true` and are excluded from `totalCredited`. The same duplicate `parentId` twice in one payload is rejected outright — combine those rows into one amount instead. Restricted to `SUPER_ADMIN`, `SCHOOL_ADMIN` and `FINANCE`.

schoolId.description: `SUPER_ADMIN` only, and required for them. Every other role is pinned to their own school; sending a different school here is rejected with 403.

reason.description: Default for every row; a row may override it.

201.description: Rows processed. Inspect `failed` — a 201 does not mean every row succeeded.

totalCredited.description: Sum of rows that actually moved money; replays excluded.

failed.error: Parent does not belong to this school

400.description: Every row failed, or the caller has no school scope

403.description: Caller may not top up parents in the requested school

422.description: Invalid body — bad amount, over 500 rows, or a duplicate parentId

post.summary: Record credit the school already holds for a parent
post.description:
Credits a parent's wallet with money the school collected outside the platform — the onboarding case where a parent has already paid ahead and that balance must offset future fees. The parent can spend it exactly like overpayment credit, via `POST /parent-wallets/me/pay`.

**Accounting:** this cash never reached the platform, so it is tracked as `externalBalance` and is deliberately excluded from the school's payable wallet when the parent spends it — otherwise the school could request a payout against funds the platform does not hold. Off-platform credit is spent before platform-held credit, so a school clears its legacy liability first. `OVERPAYMENT` is not an accepted reason here, since it would assert the platform received money it did not.

**Idempotency:** pass `reference` — the school's own receipt or ledger number. Replaying it returns the original entry with `duplicate: true` and a 200 instead of crediting twice. References are namespaced per school, so two schools reusing a receipt number never collide. Omitting it generates one, which makes a double-submit indistinguishable from two genuine credits — so send one. Restricted to `SUPER_ADMIN`, `SCHOOL_ADMIN` and `FINANCE`.

Records a payment captured outside the gateway (e.g., cash/bank transfer).

Rules:
- `schoolId` is derived from the authenticated user.
- If `paymentItemIds` contains **one** item, `receiptNumber` is used as the transaction `reference`.
- If `paymentItemIds` contains **multiple** items, `receiptNumber` is used as `groupReference` and each item gets a unique transaction `reference`.
- Transactions are recorded with `provider=MANUAL` and `status=PAID`.
- Each line may carry `amountPaid` — the cash actually collected. It defaults to the amount due.
  Anything collected **above** the amount due is credited to the parent's wallet and can be
  applied to future payments for any of that parent's children at this school; the response
  reports the banked total as `surplusCredited`. `amountPaid` below the amount due is rejected —
  this endpoint books a closing payment per item, so part payments belong on
  `/payments/manual-allocations`.

post.summary: Record a manual payment as one or more partial allocations
post.description:
Records a manual (offline) payment for a single student and splits the total across
one or more payment items as partial or full allocations in a single atomic operation.

Rules:
- `totalAmountPaid` must be greater than 0, this is the total amount paid by the user offline (which is not captured by payment gateway) and split among payment items.
- `schoolId` is derived from the authenticated user (staff only).
- `referenceNumber` is used as the `groupReference` for every created transaction;
  each per-item transaction reference is `"{referenceNumber}:{paymentItemId}"`.
- The sum of all `allocations[].amountAllocated` MUST NOT exceed `totalAmountPaid` (±0.01 tolerance).
  Allocating **less** than was collected is allowed — the unallocated remainder is credited to the
  parent's wallet and counted in `surplusCredited`, so a parent who pays ahead can have the balance
  applied to future payments.
- Allocations with `amountAllocated <= 0` are ignored. At least one positive allocation is required.
- Each allocation is capped by the item's current outstanding balance. Allocating **more** than an
  item owes is allowed: the item takes what it needs and the excess is credited to the parent's
  wallet, where it can be applied to future payments for any of that parent's children at the same
  school. The response reports the banked total as `surplusCredited`. An allocation against an item
  that is already fully settled records no transaction and goes entirely to the wallet.
- An allocation that fully clears the remaining balance is flagged `closesPaymentItem=true` and
  participates in the partial unique index — preventing duplicate closing payments per student/item.
- The optional `status` field per allocation is accepted for client convenience but is **ignored**;
  transaction status is always derived (`PAID`) and the per-item status is recomputed from totals.

post.summary: Initiate student payment(s) (batch)
post.description:
Initiates **one provider checkout** for multiple (student, paymentItem) pairs and records **one transaction per pair**.

## Request formats
This endpoint accepts **two** request body formats. Pick whichever suits your frontend best — both are fully supported.

### 1. Explicit payments array (**recommended**)
Send a `payments` array where each element explicitly maps one student to one payment item. There is **no ambiguity** — each pair is exactly what you mean.
```json {
  "payments": [
    { "studentId": "<studentA>", "paymentItemId": "<itemX>" },
    { "studentId": "<studentB>", "paymentItemId": "<itemX>" },
    { "studentId": "<studentA>", "paymentItemId": "<itemY>" }
  ],
  "callbackUrl": "https://example.com/callback"
} ```
This is the clearest way to handle scenarios like: - Same item for multiple children. - Multiple items for the same child. - Any arbitrary combination of students and items.

### 2. Legacy parallel arrays (backward-compatible)
Send `studentIds` and `paymentItemIds` arrays. Pairs are built using implicit rules:
| `studentIds.length` | `paymentItemIds.length` | Behaviour | |---|---|---| | N | N (same length) | Paired by index: `studentIds[0]` ↔ `paymentItemIds[0]`, etc. | | N | 1 | The single payment item is applied to **all** students (broadcast). | | 1 | M | The single student is charged for **all** payment items (broadcast). | | N | M (N ≠ M, both > 1) | **400 error** — ambiguous pairing. |
```json {
  "studentIds": ["<studentA>", "<studentB>"],
  "paymentItemIds": ["<itemX>"],
  "callbackUrl": "https://example.com/callback"
} ```

## How it works
1. Validates that all students and payment items exist and belong to the school. 2. Checks that the authenticated parent has access to all referenced students. 3. Computes the total amount across all pairs (applying any active discounts). 4. Creates a single checkout session with the payment provider. 5. Records one PENDING transaction per pair — each with a unique reference but sharing a `groupReference`. 6. Returns the payment URL and list of transactions.

get.summary: List transactions grouped by student
get.description:
Returns the same transactions as `GET /payments/transactions`, with the same search and filters, but grouped under the student who owes them — one row per student, carrying the student's billing totals plus the array of their matching payments. Built for a collapsible list: the header shows total paid / total outstanding at a glance, the expanded body shows the individual payments.

**Pagination is by student.** `limit: 20` returns 20 students with *all* of their matching payments attached, so a student's payments are never split across two pages. `meta.total` is the number of matching students, not transactions.

**The two totals answer different questions:**
- `totalAmountPaid` / `totalOutstanding` / `totalBilled` describe the student's whole fee
  position for the academic period (defaulting to every period when `academicPeriod` is
  omitted). They are **not** narrowed by the `status` or `category` filters, so filtering to
  `PENDING` does not zero out what the student has already paid.

- `paymentsTotalAmount` is the sum of the `payments` array actually returned, which is what
  the expanded list adds up to.


**Students who have not paid are listed too.** Rows come from the enrolled roster (narrowed by `classId` / `search`) plus any student with a matching transaction, so on the first day of a term every student appears with their full balance and `payments: []`. Setting `status` or `category` (which describe payments) or `onlyWithTransactions=true` restores the old behaviour of listing only students with a matching transaction.

**Arrears.** When `academicPeriod` is set, `totalOutstanding` / `outstanding` include `arrears` — what is still owed on fees from earlier periods. `termOutstanding` is the selected period's balance alone.

Students with payments come first, ordered by their most recent matching transaction (newest first); students with none follow alphabetically (`lastTransactionAt: null`). **Upsert behaviour:** If a discount already exists for the same `paymentItem`, it is replaced

- `FLAT` — fixed naira amount subtracted. A value of `500` means ₦500 off.

**Amount floor:** The effective amount after all discounts is never below ₦0.

post.description:
Bulk promotes all active students in the school to their next respective class.

Only classes **owned by the authenticated school** are promotion candidates, and
`classMappings` may only reference classes the school owns.

**Progression Resolution Logic:**
1. **Explicit Mappings (Top Priority):** If `classMappings` is supplied in the request body (e.g. `[{ fromClassId, toClassId }]`), the specified `toClassId` is directly assigned. Both ids must belong to this school.
2. **Automatic Level Hierarchy:** Otherwise, the system ranks the school's classes and picks the immediate next rank. Ranking uses `orderIndex` when **every** class in the school has a positive one; otherwise the whole set is ranked by name:
   `Creche (1) -> Nursery 1-3 (2-4) -> Basic 1-6 / Primary 1-6 (5-10) -> JSS 1-3 (11-13) -> SSS 1-3 (14-16)`.
   The basis actually used is returned as `rankingBasis`. Mixing the two scales produced wrong targets, so the choice is now all-or-nothing.
3. **Arm / SubClass Matching:** If the source class has an arm/subClass (e.g. `JSS 1A`), the system attempts to match the target class with the same subClass (`JSS 2A`); if not found, it falls back to the base target class. Ties are broken deterministically, so a dry run and the real run always agree.
4. **Terminal Class Handling:** Students in the highest class (e.g. `SSS 3`) are flagged with status `TERMINAL_LEVEL` and remain in their current class.

**Fee inheritance:** each promoted student records the class they are leaving against
`academicPeriodId` (the outgoing session, defaulting to the school's active period).
Fee applicability is resolved against that record, so a promoted student inherits their
new class's fees for the new term, keeps any unpaid balance from the old class, and is
not billed the new term's fees for the class they left.

**Exclusions, safety & dry run:**
- `excludeStudentIds`: Array of student ObjectIds (e.g. repeaters) to omit from promotion. `totalSkipped` counts only ids that matched an active student of this school.
- `dryRun: true`: Generates and returns the promotion projection without mutating database records.
- Promotion is not idempotent. A second run against the same period returns **409** unless `force: true` is passed.

classMappings.description: Custom overrides mapping source class IDs to target class IDs.

dryRun.description: If true, returns the promotion projection without mutating database records.

academicPeriodId.description: The session the students are leaving, recorded against each promoted student so their outgoing class stays attached to that term's fees. Defaults to the school's active period, which is correct when promoting before the new session is opened. Pass it explicitly if the new session has already been activated.

force.description: Allows a repeat promotion against a period that has already been promoted out of.

200.description: Students promoted successfully or dry-run preview generated
